derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate);
def: to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote

occurrences.text: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
